title: U.S. Open Memory IP (compiler service -> gain-cell & ReRAM macros)
status_reason: The red team killed both T2 legs. C-32 (gain cell) and C-22 (ReRAM) have no named buyer and no density or leakage case on sky130, and C-22's magnet-immunity axis is shared by OTP, eFuse and S130's own embedded NVM. The C-33 wedge survives on revised inputs: 228 projects/yr and a 55-account cap; the licence restated to nominal-lot data at $12k; free GF180 macros in the base case; a $150/h exclusive contractor; and cash-gated spends. On those inputs BASE ARR is $41.2k at m18 and $65.7k at m36, and the founder is never paid in BASE, GLUT or SEVERE. It is DOWNGRADED rather than KILLED because it needs no outside capital, is cash-positive from m12, and a ~$9.1k day-30 test decides it cheaply.

revised_verdicts.possible: Yes at simulation level for the C-33 wedge: a 1 KB sky130 macro is silicon-verified (TRL 6), while 16 KB+ macros are unproven and now gated on contractor-signed extracted-SPICE corners plus a 1,000-point Monte Carlo. An MPW can deliver 'nominal lot measured, corners simulated', not 'measured PVT corners'. No for T2 on this PDK: a logic-rule gain cell does not beat the pushed-rule 6T, and ReRAM's axis is shared by OTP and S130 eNVM.
revised_verdicts.profitable: No as a job; marginal as a side line. Gross margin is 57%, and the business is cash-positive from m12 with the founder unpaid. ARR is $41.2k at m18 and $65.7k at m36 ($164.1k run-rate), and the founder is never paid in BASE, GLUT or SEVERE: peak GP is $8.0k/mo against the $11.85k needed. Only a combined upside (price x1.3, close x1.3, no free release) pays the founder, at m22. A full free release cuts ARR at m36 to $34.0k.
revised_verdicts.doable: Yes for the wedge part-time (automation, CI, portal and sales are the founder's skills), but only with a contract memory engineer under a signed 12-month exclusivity, or a technical cofounder with equity, by m3, because the founder cannot judge the sign-off they sell. No for T2 (killed).

ev_note: For this founder the expected value is small and bounded. The strengthened day-30 test needs 2 open-PDK commercial or SBIR LOIs of $10k or more, a contractor-signed extracted-SPICE and Monte Carlo pass, and written no-release statements from both UCSC VLSIDA and OCD. I estimate it passes with ~15-25% probability. If it passes, revised BASE builds ~$7-8k a month of gross profit by m36 and ~$88k of cash for ~15 hours a week, but never a salary within 36 months; only a combined upside case pays the founder, at m22. If it fails, the loss is ~$9k, and the cash gate keeps the $40k from going negative. Net EV is about +$5-15k over three years (p x $88k - (1-p) x $9k at p = 0.15-0.25) before counting the founder's ~15 h/week [ESTIMATE]. Role: side line only. It is not PRIMARY. It is not FALLBACK, because it is not a path to full-time income. It is not a MOONSHOT candidate: T2 is killed and the wedge ceiling is ~$0.42M/yr. Run it beside the primary pick only if the founder wants open-silicon side income, and drop it on any failed day-30 rule. [Phase 7 gate correction: 04_DEEPDIVES/open-memory-ip.md §14.5 now states the expected value as about −$0.5k to +$5.3k; an earlier '+$5–15k' figure counted the founder's own $40k of starting cash as gain.]

responses.response: Accepted. A 16 h desk review of simulated Liberty files was an opinion gate. My searches found only a 1 KB silicon-verified OpenRAM sky130 macro (NSF PAR 10495552) and 4/8 KB OpenRAM test-chip configurations taped out on MPW-3 in 2021, with no published measurements of the larger ones. So the gap is real, and so is the buildability risk. Test (iii) now requires, before 2026-12-01, a contractor-signed post-layout extracted SPICE read/write of a 16 KB sky130 macro at SS/1.62 V/125 C and FF/1.98 V/-40 C, with a bitcell Monte Carlo of 1,000 points or more. If the sky130 SRAM special-device models lack usable mismatch data, (iii) fails. Contractor time rises from 16 h to 40 h ($6.0k at the revised $150/h), and the kill test from ~$5.1k to ~$9.1k, still under the $10k cap and now carried in the model at m1. Pre-silicon macros are sold labelled 'simulated, not silicon-proven'. This does not remove the silicon risk at m11/m24, but the business no longer sells on an opinion.
responses.action: Rewrote section 10 step 1 and pass rule (iii) to require extracted-SPICE corners plus a 1,000-point Monte Carlo. Kill-test budget $5.1k -> $9.1k, added to the model at m1 (R15: +$8.1k kill-test item). Section 4 preview library labelled 'simulated, not silicon-proven'.

responses.response: Accepted; this is the same finding as RT-PHY-DD5-01 and RT-HYP-DD5-02. An MPW gives one typical lot with no FF/SS/FS/SF skew wafers, and buying skew-corner wafers is not a T0 option. The plan now says plainly 'TT measured, corners simulated': one nominal lot measured at voltage and temperature points, process corners simulated and correlated to that lot, yield on 50 or more die, and a warranty limited to re-delivery or a refund of fees. The licence is repriced from $20k to $12k, and attach falls from 0.25 to 0.15 licences per commercial account a year. Thermal forcing (ThermoStream-class rental, ~$2.5k per campaign [ESTIMATE]) and BIST/delay-line test structures are now in the model. The licence's edge over free is honestly smaller, so the line falls to about $0.9k a month at m36 in revised BASE.

responses.response: Accepted; same finding as RT-PHY-DD5-03/04. A novel 2T/3T cell on an open MPW gets the standard logic DRC deck. My rough sky130 logic-rule estimate for an NMOS-only 3T cell is 2.0-2.5 um2 before refresh logic [ESTIMATE, not a layout], against the 1.896 um2 pushed-rule 6T. My own Phase 4 notes said 'near parity unless the foundry grants rule waivers'. Retention at 85-125 C in the microsecond-to-millisecond range makes 'drop-in SRAM' false. C-32 is killed on this PDK. If it is ever revived, the first deliverable is your test: a logic-rule DRC-clean layout of 1.58 um2 or less with simulated retention of 100 us or more at 125 C. PHY's 1 ms at 85 C and power test come next, all before any STTR proposal.

responses.response: Accepted on qualification, with one factual correction. The Cadence SKY130 MPW did offer a Weebit-ReRAM process option at $10-12k per block for its 2026 run (deadline 2026-01-16, die Jul-2026, per the SkyWater/Cadence page in the Phase 4 notes [REPORTED]). So a prototype path existed, but no 2027 run is documented. On qualification you are right. JESD47 needs HTOL 1,000 h on 3 lots x 77 units, plus cycled and uncycled retention bakes, ESD/latch-up and MSL, on a production S130+ReRAM flow: three engineering lots, 9-12 months, and a trusted package/test flow. $950k buys a mask set and perhaps one lot. The qualification line is revised from $400k to ~$1.0M, so the chiplet line goes from $0.95M to ~$1.55M [ESTIMATE]. Together with RT-PHY-DD5-05 and RT-VC-DD5-02, C-22 is killed.

responses.response: Accepted; my Phase 4 notes already said a logic-rule gain cell 'may land near parity'. A rough sky130 logic-rule count for an NMOS-only 3T cell is ~3 contacted poly pitches x two diffusion rows, about 2.0-2.5 um2 before refresh periphery. That is ~0.75-0.95x the density of the 1.896 um2 pushed-rule 6T [ESTIMATE, not a layout]. The BIU 1.25-1.43x compares cells drawn to the same rules. Scheduling the density check after a $305k STTR was backwards. With no density case, C-32 is killed on sky130. Revival requires a standard-DRC-clean layout of 1.58 um2 or less, including its share of read-reference and refresh periphery, produced before any proposal (~16 contract h, ~$2.4k, not funded).
responses.action: C-32 leg killed. Section 2.1 gain-cell row annotated with the logic-rule estimate. Section 11 #10 rewritten as a revival gate with the logic-DRC layout test first.

responses.response: Accepted. At 130 nm, 6T standby leakage is small, so the gain cell's leakage advantage is small too. My own notes put 130/180 nm gain-cell retention at tens of microseconds to ~1 ms, shrinking at 85-125 C. That means constant refresh and lost availability. A density-only gate would have passed a cell with tens of microseconds of retention at 85 C. C-32 is killed. The revival gate also requires 1 ms or more of worst-bit retention at 85 C (post-layout Monte Carlo or silicon), and refresh plus leakage power below measured sky130 6T standby at 16 KB or more.
responses.action: C-32 leg killed. Section 11 #10 adds the retention and power conditions. Section 2.8 states the reason.

responses.response: Accepted. SkyWater's 2025-07-29 Infineon IP release says S130 already offers embedded NVM options alongside its SRAM compilers (the snippet does not name the technology). Antifuse/eFuse OTP also covers provisioning-time keys; the Tillitis/Zedulo GF180 chip already uses eFUSE. Everspin's AN02049 gives 8,000 A/m write immunity for 16 Mb parallel parts and 12,000 A/m for serial. ReRAM adds forming, write-verify, ECC and high-temperature drift. No named buyer states a field requirement above 8,000 A/m plus a rewrite need. C-22 is killed.

responses.response: Accepted. The free OpenRAM macros sit at 8-11% array efficiency. Going from the 1 KB to the 2 KB OpenRAM sky130 macro adds 11.5 um2 per added bit, 6.0x the bitcell (model section 1), so the periphery does not amortise like a commercial compiler's. The even row/column rule and the strap and dummy cells cut efficiency further. The assumption is cut from 60% to 30% until measured, so the claim falls from 316.5 to 158.2 kbit/mm2 (5.5x to 2.7x the 2 KB macro). The day 1-20 run must report the real area of a DRC/LVS-clean 32 KB macro. If it is under 2x the 2 KB density (~115 kbit/mm2), the density pitch to FABulous-class buyers is dropped.
